title: kv-cache: improved eviction/paging/spillover heuristics to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Priya Desai
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring OOMs and degraded tail-latency under mixed-length workloads caused by KV cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover paging. This PR introduces a set of coordinated changes to memory accounting, eviction ordering, spillover paging thresholds, and compaction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, avoid pathological paging under high-concurrency, and improve steady-state throughput.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce age-and-density scoring for eviction (prefer evicting dense cold regions before scattering hot entries); 2) Add adaptive spillover threshold that increases reservation during high-concurrency spikes to avoid frequent page thrashing; 3) Background compaction pass that coalesces small KV fragments when free-run > 50ms; 4) Minor scheduler tweak to prefer batching requests that share KV pages to reduce concurrent page faults; 5) Telemetry hooks and new perf counters for fragmentation, page-fault-rate, and compaction-time.

Testing & benchmarks: Microbenchmarks with synthetic mixture (tokens-per-request distribution from production traces) show a 22-35% reduction in tail token latency (p95-p99) and 18% lower memory churn under sustained 10k rps scenarios. Integration tests cover eviction correctness, spillover boundary conditions, and compaction idempotency.

Risk & rollout: Changes are behind a runtime flag and gated by canary rollout. The adaptive threshold defaults to conservative values; we provided a migration doc and metrics alerts if compaction time or page-fault-rate regresses.
